items.text: Oil prices (WTI $84.25, Brent $91.82) have reversed sharply lower from peaks, but a ~25% surge followed Mid-East escalation in recent weeks. Energy inflation remains +15.7% YoY despite June's -5.7% monthly print. Refiners & energy-exposed credit face renewed volatility; near-term pressure on corporate spreads if geopolitical shocks persist.

Initial claims at 187k (7/18) show tightness, but payrolls decelerated to +57k in June vs +129k prior, and unemployment sits steady at 4.2%. Labor softening is real, yet not alarming—provides some disinflationary slack but insufficient to trigger aggressive Fed cuts near term.

Headline CPI eased to 3.46% YoY (June final) and June PCE likely ~3.7% YoY (preliminary estimates), but core inflation sticks at 2.57% CPI (June), 3.3-3.4% PCE expected. Services inflation moderated but cost-of-living sentiment remains fragile; year-ahead inflation expectations still 4.6%, well above pre-Iran 3.4%.

Fed funds locked at 3.75%, curve at 35bps (flattening). ECB deposit rate at 2.25% post-June hike, unlikely to cut through year-end per forward guidance. Higher-for-longer is the regime; Fed Chair Warsh signaled skepticism over 'mission accomplished' despite June disinflation, hinting no near-term cuts unless data deteriorates sharply.

HY OAS widened to 284bps (up 7bps), IG OAS +2bps to 81bps, CCC OAS jumped 14bps to 1005bps. Default risk is migrating toward distressed names and emerging stress points—refinancing walls, leveraged operations, and commodity hedges are stress-testing weaker credits. Valuations favor tactical entry into dislocated idiosyncratic names.

GDPNow at 1.54% (down from 2.39% forecast), a sharp deceleration from Q1's 2.1%. Chinese manufacturing in structural contraction (PMI 49.3 July); U.S. labor market softening. Late-cycle dynamics accelerating, but not yet recession-force; watch for Q2 GDP preliminary and August labor data for conviction on growth trajectory.

Mortgage rates at 6.58%, existing home sales fell to 4.09M from 4.19M (June). Consumer sentiment rebounded to 54.4 preliminary (July) on gasoline price relief, but remains 12% below year-ago levels. Housing activity fragile, refinancing constrained; consumer resilience is transitory, tied to oil prices and sentiment volatility remains a tail-risk for spending forecasts.

themeCards.title: Middle East Energy Shock Volatility
themeCards.statusLine: Oil spiked ~25% on Iran tensions but has reversed sharply lower; WTI back to $84 but refiners and traded energy credit remain whipsawed. Geopolitical tail risk has returned as a material volatility driver after Q2 lull.
themeCards.relevance: High-yield energy credits and leveraged refiners now face renewed hedging costs and margin pressure; syndicated loans tied to commodity hedges are repricing. CCC energy names in default-adjacent distress; special situations traders should scan for refinancing walls and working-capital stress in E&P.

themeCards.title: China Hard Landing Unwind
themeCards.statusLine: Official PMI 49.3 in July (below 50 for 4th month), signaling structural slowdown in China's manufacturing export engine. Domestic demand sputtering despite government support; policy response has been measured, not aggressive.
themeCards.relevance: Weakness in Chinese demand ripples through global trade; U.S. exporters and multinationals with China exposure face earnings headwinds. Distressed-credit opportunities in sectors exposed to China slowdown (industrials, materials, semiconductors) are emerging; credit widening in large-cap names provides entry points.

themeCards.title: Refinancing Wall & Floating-Rate Stress
themeCards.statusLine: High yield curve at 35bps (compressed), 10-year yields at 4.65%; corporates facing repricing of 2024–2025 maturities in a 4%+ rate environment. Floating-rate debt holders now face sustained high coupons with no cut relief near-term.
themeCards.relevance: Sponsors and levered buyout portfolios facing higher-than-expected coupons on refinanced debt; net leverage drifting higher as EBITDA growth slows. Identify credits with known 2026–2027 maturity wall exposure where sponsor equity is thin; distressed scenarios more probable.

themeCards.title: Services/Labor Soft Spot
themeCards.statusLine: ISM Services at 54.0 (June), down 0.5 from May; employment component rebounded but business activity slowing. Wage growth +3.52% YoY (June), decelerating but sticky at elevated levels.
themeCards.relevance: Labor-intensive service sectors (hospitality, healthcare, consumer discretionary) may see margin compression if revenue growth stalls. Watch for covenant stress in consumer-facing credits if spending momentum falters; services PMI employment weakness signals potential for jobless claims ticks higher.

themeCards.title: Consumer Sentiment Fragility
themeCards.statusLine: U. Michigan sentiment rebounded to 54.4 (July prelim) on gasoline relief, but remains 12% below year-ago and trapped in 44–54 range. One-year inflation expectations still 4.6%, well above pre-crisis 3.4%. Sentiment gains are transitory, vulnerable to energy repricing or labor data weakness.
themeCards.relevance: Consumer spending (2/3 of GDP) is fragile; retail data weak at +0.2% m/m in June ex-energy. Discretionary credit (auto, apparel, restaurant, retail) faces demand risk if sentiment rolls over. Track weekly jobless claims and credit-card delinquencies for early consumer stress signals; retailers with thin debt covenants are downside risks.

themeCards.title: Rates Locked Higher, Curve Flattening
themeCards.statusLine: Fed funds 3.75% with no cuts priced until 2027; Fed Chair Warsh signaled skepticism over near-term easing despite June CPI beat. Curve flattened to 35bps (2y–10y), with 10-year yields at 4.65%. Market pricing two hikes by March 2027 if inflation re-accelerates.
themeCards.relevance: Duration is a headwind for fixed-rate debt portfolios; longer-maturity debt and bonds trading at distressed discounts offer asymmetric upside if Fed does cut, but spread widening risk persists near-term. Floating-rate credit and shorter-dated maturities benefit from rate stability. Curve steepening trades and duration positioning critical for portfolio hedge.

ecb.delta: held June 17, no further hikes expected through year-end

chinaPMI.delta: July contraction below 50 for 4th straight month; June official was 50.3

ismServices.delta: June final; July release Aug 5, preliminary sentiment suggests modest softening near 53

retailSales.delta: June ex-autos weak; +0.7% m/m when adjusted for energy

existingHome.delta: June down from 4.19M; YoY decline signals demand weakness despite lower rates expected later

consensus.CPI: 3.5% YoY (June actual released 7/14); no forward consensus yet for July release (expected ~mid-August)
consensus.Payrolls: +100k–120k expected for June final revisions; July release pending late July/early August
consensus.PCE: Headline ~3.7% YoY, Core ~3.3% YoY for June (preliminary estimates); official release 7/30–7/31
consensus.PPI: 5.51% YoY (June final) vs 5.97% prior; no July consensus yet released
consensus.Retail Sales: +0.3–0.5% m/m expected for June ex-autos; July data pending early August
consensus.ISM Mfg: 53.3 in June (final); July release pending early August; market expects ~52.5–53.0
consensus.ISM Services: 54.0 in June (final); July release Aug 5; market expects 53.5–54.5
consensus.GDP: 2.1% (Q1 2026 final, released 1/30); GDPNow tracker at 1.54% for Q2; full Q2 preliminary release likely late July/early August

regime.label: Late-cycle / Volatility Creep
regime.detail: Fed locked higher-for-longer, China hard-landing unwind, energy volatility spiking, labor softening, consumer fragile, spreads widening on refinancing stress—growth deceleration with inflation sticky. Tail risks rising.
